messages.author: d674bddd91c6f700
messages.subject: one-sided limits?
parts:
If I don't specify limits for, say, scale_y_log10(), ggplot will do its best to determine sensible lower and upper limits.  I can specify both of those limits by hand, of course.  Is it possible to specify only one or the other of those limits?  (I don't believe it's possible.)  Especially for histograms, it would be nice to be able to specify just the lower limit and let ggplot figure out a suitable upper limit.  

- Dave

messages.author: d674bddd91c6f700
messages.subject: Re: one-sided limits?
parts:
I'm not sure that expand_limits does quite what I was looking for - though maybe I'm just being dense.  Its use seems to be to make the limits more expansive than they might otherwise be; I'm looking to make them less expansive.

d<-data.frame(x=rnorm(1000,10,1))
ggplot(d)+geom_histogram(aes(x=x))+scale_y_log10()

I can get most of the way to what I want with 

ggplot(d)+geom_histogram(aes(x=x))+scale_y_log10()+coord_cartesian(ylim=c(1,100))

but what I had in mind was something like 

ggplot(d)+geom_histogram(aes(x=x))+scale_y_log10()+coord_cartesian(ylim=c(1,NA))

- Dave

You are right; I misunderstood. expand_limits will only make the range
bigger. I don't know of a one-sided way to specify limits that are
smaller than the trained range.
